rp-01.a.text: The assessment rates the exposure from an automated decisioning model as if none of the review, threshold or appeal mechanisms existed.
rp-01.a.why: Inherent risk is the gross position before controls. It exists to size the control effort. Acceptance is judged against residual risk; the two figures only coincide when the organisation knowingly retains the risk with no treatment at all.
rp-01.b.text: The assessment rates the same model with review, thresholds and appeal operating as designed, and reports what remains.
rp-01.b.why: Residual risk is what sign-off is actually against. Accepting against the inherent figure over-states what the organisation has agreed to carry.

rp-02.a.text: The board states that the organisation will not pursue AI applications that make consequential decisions about individuals without human review.
rp-02.a.why: Appetite is the broad, forward-looking statement of what risk the organisation is willing to take in pursuit of its objectives.
rp-02.b.text: The policy states that a model may go live only if subgroup accuracy disparity is below four percentage points.
rp-02.b.why: Tolerance is the measurable boundary that operationalises appetite. That limit-setting reading follows COSO usage, where the 2017 framework speaks of acceptable variation in performance; ISO Guide 73 frames tolerance as readiness to bear a risk after treatment. Appetite without tolerance cannot be tested; tolerance without appetite is arbitrary.

rp-03.a.text: The model can produce fluent, confident text that is factually wrong.
rp-03.a.why: A hazard is a potential source of harm. It belongs to the thing itself and exists before you ask who is exposed or how it is used, even though how often it shows up can still vary with retrieval, prompting and domain.
rp-03.b.text: Because the model drafts patient discharge instructions read by non-specialists, confident errors may lead to incorrect medication use.
rp-03.b.why: Risk combines the hazard with exposure and consequence in a context. The same hazard is a different risk in a different deployment — which is why tiers attach to use.

rp-04.a.text: Input validation rejects requests containing patterns that the system is not authorised to process.
rp-04.a.why: Preventive controls act on likelihood, before the event. They are the only kind that can bring a probability meaningfully toward zero.
rp-04.b.text: A weekly report lists requests that were processed despite falling outside authorised categories.
rp-04.b.why: Detective controls act on duration and impact after the fact. A register listing detective controls as mitigation of likelihood over-states its position.

rp-05.a.text: The AI governance team reviews the delivery team's impact assessment and challenges its conclusions, reporting to the chief risk officer.
rp-05.a.why: Independent of delivery but still inside management. Second line advises, challenges and monitors; it cannot provide assurance on itself.
rp-05.b.text: A review function examines whether those governance reviews were carried out as policy requires, and reports to the audit committee.
rp-05.b.why: Reporting to the board rather than to management is the structural difference. Without it, assurance is self-assessment with a different letterhead.

rp-06.a.text: The team adds an automated evaluation gate that blocks releases failing the robustness threshold.
rp-06.a.why: Likelihood falls because a failing release cannot ship. Something about the risk itself changed.
rp-06.b.text: The team adds a dashboard showing robustness scores, and agrees to review them monthly with no gating.
rp-06.b.why: Watching a risk is not treating it. Monitoring plus a decision not to gate is retention with better visibility — legitimate, provided it is recorded as acceptance.

rp-07.a.text: A general-purpose model exceeding the compute threshold must undergo adversarial testing and report serious incidents.
rp-07.a.why: Systemic-risk GPAI duties attach to the model regardless of any downstream use, which is why they sit outside the risk pyramid.
rp-07.b.text: A deployer using that same model to screen job applicants must meet high-risk obligations for the deployment.
rp-07.b.why: The tier follows the purpose. One model can simultaneously carry model-level duties and sit in several different use tiers.

rp-08.a.text: A contract makes the vendor liable for the cost of damages arising from defects in the model they supplied.
rp-08.a.why: Financial consequence moves. This is a legitimate treatment and it changes nothing about the harm's likelihood.
rp-08.b.text: The regulator holds the deploying firm answerable for the outcomes of the decisions it makes with that vendor's model.
rp-08.b.why: Regulatory accountability generally cannot be contracted away. Assuming an indemnity covers it is the most expensive version of this confusion.
